newsitem.title: JAPAN: No cause for concern on Japan economy--MOF's Kato.
newsitem.headline: No cause for concern on Japan economy--MOF's Kato.

text.p: There is no cause for concern about the health of the Japanese economy, Vice Finance Minister for International Affairs Takatoshi Kato said in an interview.

Commenting on the key "tankan" quarterly business survey released by the Bank of Japan last week, he said: "The market interpretation is that the tankan released recently was better than the market had expected."
Kato's comments were made in a recorded interview with Reuters Financial Television in the Philippines on Saturday.
Asked why Japan's long-term interest rates have fallen despite an improvement in the business outlook, Kato said: "It is very difficult to pin down the causes."

He added: "(Regarding) movements of long-term interest rates, I don't know, some institutional aspects may have something to do with that or simply, I think, Japanese government bonds are very popular among Japanese investors."
Asked if there was any concern about the Japanese economy, he said, "I don't think so."

Kato also said the ratio of the surplus in Japan's current account, the broadest measure of trade in goods and services, to the country's gross domestic product (GDP) is smaller than the ratios in Germany and France.

"Japan's balance in goods and services trade in the GDP stood at 0.5 percent last year. Obviously fluctuations could arise from time to time, but I think it is still smaller, compared with that of France and Germany," he said.
The Finance Ministry announced on Monday that Japan's current account surplus rose 15.4 percent to 865.2 billion yen in February from a year earlier.
